missing_diagram_candidates.classification: editorial candidate; not a confirmed defect
missing_diagram_candidates.rationale: The defining formula maps each output site to a translated, stride-scaled receptive field, applies per-offset channel-mixing matrices, and uses a boundary extension. A small lattice sketch would expose the indexing convention and the difference between cross-correlation and mathematical convolution.
missing_diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Draw a few input lattice sites with domain D, one output site p in O, its anchor a+s⊙p, and offsets δ∈K mapped to x̃(a+s⊙p+δ). Mark one padded site outside D as zero for zero padding, label each W_δ as C_in×C_out, and show output b plus the weighted row-vector sum. If comparing with mathematical convolution, show offset reversal explicitly.

missing_diagram_candidates.classification: editorial candidate; not a confirmed defect
missing_diagram_candidates.rationale: The theorem emphasizes a finite recurrence with the same parameter θ used at each transition and a reverse sweep that sums every transition pullback. A graph can clarify why the parameter gradient is accumulated across uses and why the T=0 boundary case leaves only direct and initial-state terms.
missing_diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Draw θ→h₀ and for each t, (θ,h_{t−1})→h_t, followed by (θ,h_T)→J. In the reverse view, label λ_T=(D_hℓ)^T and λ_{t−1}=B_t^Tλ_t; send each A_t^Tλ_t arrow to one shared θ accumulator, then add (D_θℓ)^T and (Dh₀)^Tλ₀. Mark the transition-sum empty when T=0. Ensure the diagram is explanatory only; the proof remains the chain rule.
